title: First launch offers the tour or gets out of your way
goal: A new person should be able to say "show me around" or "let me at it", once, and never be asked again. After the one time permissions setup the Welcome window already does, offer two clear ways on: take the tour, or skip and start working. Whichever is picked is remembered, the tour is always reachable later from Help, and nobody is ever nagged.
notes:
Depends on the framework task, and reads the Take the Tour guide it ships.

The existing flow is in Sources/Photonz/Welcome/WelcomeController.swift. Two things there decide how this is built:
- completedDefaultsKey is "welcome.setupCompleted", and presentIfNeeded only presents while that is false. "Finished" means the window was closed with Screen Recording granted (see the type's own doc comment). Do not tangle the tour choice with that condition: somebody who grants permission and skips the tour must count as finished, or the window comes back every launch.
- The window is presented 600ms after launch and takes focus. A tour that starts by taking focus a second time, or that starts before there is a document window to point at, will feel broken. Work out the handoff and record it.

The empty-editor onboarding card (Sources/Photonz/EditorView.swift:590-615) already tells a new person how to get an image in. That is the same audience this offer is talking to, so the two must not both be shouting. Deciding which one owns that moment is part of this task.

Do not add a second "would you like a tour" prompt anywhere else in the app later. One offer, one remembered answer, always reachable from Help.

---
SHARED CONTEXT for every tutorials task (asked for by the user on 2026-09-12):

The user's words: "I would like a help > tutorials > * set of guides which walks you through basics of various features. Maybe a nice getting started tutorial, maybe a 'building components' walkthrough, etc. ... And maybe a first run experience which lets you get an intro to the app, or just gogogo. Use the design clickthroughs as inspiration, where you have pointers and can point to various parts of the application. Build a nice framework for defining these walkthroughs so that we can extend it over time. I'd like the tutorials system to be well organized and not just a long list of things."

The agreed shape (settled in the intake conversation, 2026-09-12):
- TRACKS, not a flat list. Help > Tutorials holds "Take the Tour" plus one SUBMENU per track, and a Tutorials window is the hub. The tracks are: Basics, Redlining, Looks, Colours & Styles, Building UI, Components, Video.
- A guide is DATA, not code: a Codable value in PhotonzCore describing steps. Adding a guide means adding data to the catalogue, and the menu, the window and the progress list all pick it up with no UI edited. That is the whole point of the framework and the thing that makes it extensible.
- Steps POINT AT REAL UI, clickthrough-style: a callout with a pointer aimed at a named control, not a page of prose.
- Design doc: docs/design/tutorials.md is the source of truth for the framework and the track list, written by the foundation task and extended by the rest.

THE TRAP that will waste a runner's day if it is not read first: the app already has a registry of named UI targets, the playtest harness (playtestControl / playtestField / steady names, Sources/Photonz/Playtest/PanelTarget.swift). It looks like exactly the right thing to reuse and it is NOT USABLE here: it is compiled out of the shipping build (Scripts/build-app.sh defines PHOTONZ_PLAYTEST for the dev and probe variants only, see docs/design/playtest-harness.md, "Who can run it"), and PanelTarget.swift:141 onwards is the no-op stub release actually gets. Tutorials ship to users, so the anchor registry has to be its own thing that is compiled IN for release. Model it on the playtest one - especially the STEADY NAME idea at PanelTarget.swift:126-138, a name taken off the model rather than off the copy, so rewording a label cannot break a guide - but do not depend on it.

Existing surfaces a tutorial entry point must fit with rather than duplicate:
- The Welcome window (Sources/Photonz/Welcome/WelcomeController.swift), first-run permissions setup, re-reachable from the menu-bar menu as "Welcome & Permissions...". It already owns first launch.
- The empty-editor onboarding card (Sources/Photonz/EditorView.swift:590-615): open a file, capture a rectangle, paste an image, blank canvas.
- There is NO Help menu in the app today: EditorCommands.swift declares Capture, Image, Video, Layer and the standard groups, and macOS supplies the default Help menu. Help > Tutorials has to be created.

Queue-driven app work targets the NEXT release unless the task says otherwise (CLAUDE.md), and a Current change is not finished until Next has it.
acceptance: On a genuinely first launch, after permissions are sorted, the choice is offered once: take the tour, or skip and get going
Skipping is a real answer: the offer does not come back on the next launch, and nothing nags later
Taking the tour starts the tour guide in a real window with something in it, not on an empty canvas with nothing to point at
The choice lives in the existing Welcome window rather than a second welcome surface, and Welcome and Permissions... still works exactly as it does now when reopened later
The empty editor onboarding card and this offer do not both appear at once saying overlapping things; say in the audit how they were made to agree
Tested from a clean slate: the defaults key is cleared and the whole first run is walked, captured in the audit
An upgrade from a version that had no tutorials does not re-present first-run setup to somebody who already finished it
Audit under queue/audits/ with the first-run sequence captured, and anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note:
Adversarial review of the idea, before building.

Walked the real first run rather than the happy one, and four of the five traps are in the sequence itself, not in the UI:

1. THE RELAUNCH TRAP. On a genuinely fresh Mac the setup window does not end in a ready state, it ends in "Relaunch Photonz": a Screen Recording grant only takes effect in a fresh process (WelcomeState.needsRelaunch). Offering a tour there starts a walkthrough that a relaunch kills twenty seconds later. So the choice waits for granted AND no relaunch pending, and the offer lands on the launch AFTER the relaunch, which is also the first launch where the app actually works.

2. THE NAG TRAP. The obvious build is "present the window while the tour offer is unanswered", and that re-opens it every launch for anybody who never reaches an answerable state. Two guards: the choice only appears once Screen Recording is sorted, and CLOSING the window in that state IS the answer, skip. Somebody who never grants sees exactly today behaviour and no new nag.

3. THE UPGRADE TRAP. Widening the launch condition at all re-presents first run setup to every existing user, who finished it months ago. A one time migration stamps anyone who already completed setup as answered before the condition is ever read, keyed so it can only happen once.

4. THE MIGRATION EATS THE NEW USER. The naive migration (setup completed and no answer, so stamp skip) fires on the fresh user the moment they relaunch, because by then setup IS completed. That is the quiet bug in this task. The stamp is therefore one time on the first tutorials aware launch, so a fresh install is stamped nothing on its very first launch and the offer survives the relaunch.

5. FOCUS. The setup window is a floating panel above every editor window. A tour started while it is up points at controls behind it. Close first, then start, which is the rule the Tutorials window already follows.

The mock question, the empty editor onboarding card: the task says the two must not both shout. They cannot. PhotonzApp uses a WindowGroup, so no window is forced open at launch, and the card only exists inside an editor window with nothing in it. They are sequential rather than simultaneous: the offer asks "shall I show you around", the card answers "how do I get a picture in". Take the Tour opens the guide own sample window, which has a picture in it, so the card is not there either. No suppression logic, because suppressing the card would leave an empty canvas with no help at all, which is worse than the thing being avoided.

Cut as decorative: a "Maybe later" third button, a "do not show this again" tick, a tour preview thumbnail, and a second offer anywhere else in the app. Two buttons, one remembered answer, Help for ever after.

Shortest version that delivers the same value: one pure decision type with tests, one defaults key, a footer that grows two buttons in the ready state, one migration. No new window and no new surface.

Built and verified. What landed:

PhotonzCore, FirstRunOffer.swift (pure, 19 new tests): when the question is asked, what closing the window means, what an install that predates tutorials gets, and the three pieces of copy. The tests drive the sequence LAUNCH BY LAUNCH through a tiny model of the two things that persist, because every trap in this task is in the order of a real first run rather than in the UI.

App: the setup window (WelcomeController, WelcomeView) gained the offer, a defaults key for the answer, a one time migration stamp, and a handoff that closes the window before starting the guide. AppCoordinator wires Take the Tour to TutorialLauncher with no editor, so the guide opens its own sample window.

Playtest: TutorialHubProbe split into WindowReadProbe (any window, read and pressed through the accessibility tree) plus the two windows that use it, and nine new walk actions so a first run can be driven from a clean slate without relaunching the app. Scripts/playtest/first-run-walk.json walks all three endings.

Two things found by running it rather than by reading it, both fixed:
1. Two buttons beside the shortcut caption squeezed it onto three wrapped lines and made the moment of choosing look busy. The footer now stacks in the offer state, caption above, buttons on their own row.
2. The header said "You are all set" eight lines above a green card already saying "You're all set here". Reworded to "Everything is ready", which is the same news said once.

Adversarial review of the BUILT thing, on the real app (Scripts/playtest/first-run-walk.json, 31 steps, two real screen captures with the Screen Recording grant).

What is good: the question is one line and two buttons, the two buttons are the only things in the footer so the eye lands on them, Take the Tour really does close the setup window before the guide starts (checked, not assumed: the walk fails if the panel is still up over the window it opened), and all three endings are silent on every launch after.

What is clumsy, and is filed or said out loud rather than hidden:
- The tour leaves you sitting in its sample picture when it ends, which on a genuine first run is the only window you have. Filed p2 (the-tour-leaves-you-sitting-in-its-sample-pictur): it is the end of a guide, not the start, and it happens the same way from Help.
- Somebody who never turns on Screen Recording is never offered the tour, because the offer waits for the permissions to work. Filed p2 as a question rather than a bug (find-out-whether-somebody-who-never-turns-on-scr): the guard is deliberate and written down, and the bigger version of the question is what the app should do for somebody who will not give it the screen.
- The finished permission steps still fill most of the window while the question is one line at the top. I considered collapsing them and decided against it: hiding what somebody has just done, at the moment they have just done it, reads as the app throwing their work away. Put in the audit as a question for the user instead of decided quietly.

Acceptance, item by item, all verified rather than assumed:
1. Offered once after permissions are sorted: FirstRunOffer.showsChoice waits on granted and no pending restart; walk steps 2 to 5 and capture 1.
2. Skipping is a real answer: the walk presses Start Working then runs the real launch hook twice more, and expectNoWelcome fails the walk if anything comes up. It did not.
3. The tour starts in a real window with something in it: capture 2, the Tutorial Sample window with the starter screen and the guide on step 1 of 6. The walk fails if no such window opens.
4. It lives in the existing Welcome window, and reopening from the menu is unchanged: new walk action showWelcomeAgain reads the reopened window back and fails if either offered button is in it. The log reads "Button: Start Capturing", which is exactly today.
5. The card and the offer cannot both appear: PhotonzApp uses a WindowGroup so no window is forced open at launch, and the tour opens a window with a picture already in it. Said in the audit and written into docs/design/tutorials.md.
6. Clean slate: freshInstall forgets all three settings and the walk runs the real launch hook, so the whole first run is walked rather than simulated.
7. An upgrade is not re-presented: oldInstall plus launchHook plus expectNoWelcome in the walk, and checked against the real machine, where com.dzearing.photonz.dev and com.dzearing.photonz both already have welcome.setupCompleted = 1, so the stamp marks them answered on their first launch of this build.
8. Audit at queue/audits/2026-09-12-first-run-offer.json with both captures beside it.

Scripts/test.sh green at 5824. The tutorial walks (3) and the new first run walk all pass. Asked for a sweep, because the setup window now presents on a wider condition and the harness probe was renamed.

A new person is asked once, in the setup window that already owns first launch: one line under the title, Take the Tour or Start Working in the footer, and whichever is pressed is remembered for good. The question waits until the macOS permissions actually work, closing the window counts as skip so nobody is nagged, and a one time stamp keeps an upgrade from ever seeing first run setup again. Take the Tour closes the window then opens the guide's own sample window, so the tour never starts on an empty canvas. Rules are pure in PhotonzCore/FirstRunOffer.swift with 19 tests; Scripts/test.sh green at 5824; walked from a clean slate end to end by Scripts/playtest/first-run-walk.json (31 steps, all three endings, two real screen captures). Docs in docs/design/tutorials.md, audit at queue/audits/2026-09-12-first-run-offer.json, two rough edges filed p2.
